## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Established always-on person-detection task for edge vision.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Connects object annotations to a compact binary vision pipeline. |
| **Systems behavior** | Mobile convolution, image preprocessing, and single-stream latency. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | Direct MLPerf Tiny workload inheritance. |
| **Model choice** | MobileNetV1 is fixed by the upstream MLPerf Tiny contract. |
| **Dataset choice** | The Visual Wake Words COCO derivation is fixed upstream. |
| **Quality metric** | Binary top-1 accuracy and the threshold are fixed upstream. |
| **Published baseline** | MLPerf Tiny reference quality contract |
| **Alternative rejected** | Synthetic deterministic images cannot support the upstream quality claim. |

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload visual-wake-words --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload visual-wake-words --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload visual-wake-words --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload visual-wake-words --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

| **Tolerance** | 0.0 |
| **Reference runs** | 0 |

**Reviewer notes:**

- The 80% threshold, MobileNet task, and 1,000-example balanced accuracy contract are inherited from MLPerf Tiny.
- Promotion requires committed repeated timing evidence and independent review of the TFLite-to-PyTorch adapter.
- Each execution performs five untimed complete accuracy-set passes, then measures 50 unchanged passes; quality is computed from the first measured pass only.

## Systems Experiment Execution Contract

**Within-run measurement protocol:**

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Primary metric** | inference_seconds |
| **Scenario** | offline |
| **Timing scope** | 50 repetitions of the complete 1,000-example accuracy set after model, data, and five complete-set warmup passes are ready |
| **Included phases** | batched PyTorch model execution |
| **Excluded phases** | asset fetching and exact accuracy-set selection, JPEG decoding and RGB float32 normalization, TFLite weight parsing and PyTorch model construction, one shape warmup for each observed batch shape, five untimed complete accuracy-set passes, accuracy computation, report and provenance serialization |
| **Device synchronization** | synchronize immediately before and after the measured inference region |
| **Outer reference runs** | 1 |
| **Outer preconditioning runs** | 0 |
| **Outer inter execution cooldown seconds** | 5 |
| **Repeatability metric** | inference_seconds |
| **Repeatability limit** | 0.05 |

## Results

To make the metric concrete, one run of this benchmark on Apple M5 Max observed `top1_accuracy` of 0.8510, taking 0.7174 `inference_seconds`.

That is an illustration, not a target and not a score. It comes from a single machine and your hardware will produce different timing. The number that matters is the one your own run reports.

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload visual-wake-words --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
